core:FASTFIGHTING.Story.TablesMenuHint: The hint under the Story tables button: what the button is for. It installs the Roleplay story's sentences as Rollable Tables in this world, where the GM can edit them.
core:FASTFIGHTING.Story.TablesHint: The explanation at the top of the Story tables dialog. Every sentence of the Roleplay story is rolled from tables: an action table, named by how it was delivered, the damage type and how well it went (e.g. Melee · Slashing · Minor Success), and a relationship table (e.g. Relationship · Enemy Leader · Failure). Installing them lets the GM edit them, add entries or translate them; tables installed in the world are used before the built-in ones.
core:FASTFIGHTING.Story.TablesInstalled: In the dialog, after two numbers ('12 / 40 …'): how many of the story tables are installed in this world, out of all of them.
core:FASTFIGHTING.Story.TablesLocale: A small note in the dialog for translators: a translation module can ship story/<language>.json with the same table keys, and it's used automatically for that language.
core:FASTFIGHTING.Story.Install: A button in the dialog: install the story tables this world doesn't have yet (the ones already installed are left alone).
core:FASTFIGHTING.Story.ReinstallConfirm: The are-you-sure question before 'Reinstall all': every installed story table is replaced with the built-in version, and the GM's edits to them are lost.
core:FASTFIGHTING.Story.Installing: A notice at the top of the screen while the story tables are being installed.
core:FASTFIGHTING.Story.Installed: A notice when installing is done: how many tables were installed ({created}) and how many were already there ({kept}).
core:FASTFIGHTING.Generic.Label: The name of FastFighting's generic support, used for a game system that has no FastFighting helper: shown where the planner names the game system (beside the scene's name) and in notices. It reads the system as a d20 game, from the data paths the GM set.
core:FASTFIGHTING.Generic.MenuName: The name of the button row that opens the generic system dialog: where on an actor, in a system with no helper, FastFighting finds a creature's numbers.
core:FASTFIGHTING.Generic.MenuHint: The hint under that button: it's only for game systems without a FastFighting helper module; it tells FastFighting where on an actor to find hit points, armor class, attack bonus and damage. (Your generic words for these are AC/Def and HP/Health.)
core:FASTFIGHTING.Generic.Hint: The explanation at the top of the generic system dialog: each box takes a property path on the actor (keep the example path as it is: system.attributes.hp.value). Leave attack or damage empty and FastFighting estimates them from the creature's level.
core:FASTFIGHTING.Generic.Path.ac: The label of a box in the generic system dialog: the path to a creature's armor class, or whatever defense attacks roll against.
core:FASTFIGHTING.Generic.Path.perceptio: The label of a box in the generic system dialog: the path to a creature's Perception modifier (for noticing hidden foes). Optional: without it, the initiative modifier stands in.
The name of the button row that opens the side defaults dialog: each side's default group personality.
The hint under that button: the default group values of the four personality traits (Tactical, Brave, Selfish, Loyal) for each side (Friendly, Hostile, Neutral, Secret).
core:FASTFIGHTING.Defaults.Hint: The explanation at the top of the side defaults dialog: each side's group personality. Every member's own trait values are blended with these (30% the side's, 70% its own), and the planner can fudge both for a battle.
core:FASTFIGHTING.Settings.genericFallba: A setting's name (on or off): use FastFighting's experimental generic support for a game system that has no FastFighting helper module.

The hint under it: only for systems without a FastFighting helper module; it guesses hit points, armor class, attacks and damage from the data paths set in the generic system dialog; the results will be rough.
core:FASTFIGHTING.Settings.runs.Name: A setting's name: how many fights the simulation runs each time (the Runs box in the planner starts at this).
core:FASTFIGHTING.Settings.runs.Hint: The hint under it: how many battles to simulate; more gives steadier odds but takes longer (2000, the default, takes well under a second for a typical fight). From 200 to 20,000.
core:FASTFIGHTING.Settings.maxRounds.Hin: The hint under Max rounds: a simulated battle still going after this many rounds counts as a stalemate (no one wins). Default 20; from 3 to 100.
core:FASTFIGHTING.Settings.includeHidden: A setting's name (on or off): whether hidden tokens can take part. It's the default for the planner's Hidden tokens switch.
The hint under it: hidden tokens that aren't in the encounter (ambushers, reinforcements) take part by default; the encounter's own combatants always do; the planner can change it for a battle.
core:FASTFIGHTING.Settings.includeOtherL: A setting's name (on or off): whether tokens on the scene's other Levels can take part.
The hint under it: tokens on scene Levels other than the one being viewed (and not in the encounter) can take part. Off by default.
core:FASTFIGHTING.Settings.neutralDefaul: The hint under Neutral tokens: what neutral tokens do by default. They stand on the field taking no side, perhaps leaning one way (the choices below). Whoever hurts or robs them, or crosses what they want (hurting someone they lean toward), turns them against their side, and either side's talkers can try to win them over (harder against their lean). The planner's Neutral tab can change it for a battle, and any token can be moved to another side.
core:FASTFIGHTING.Lean.exclude: A choice for neutral tokens (this setting's dropdown, and the planner's Neutral tab): they're left out of the fight entirely.
core:FASTFIGHTING.Lean.neutral: A choice for neutral tokens: on the field, taking no side, leaning nowhere, until something crosses them.
core:FASTFIGHTING.Lean.friendly: A choice for neutral tokens: taking no side, but leaning toward the party (they want the party's members safe).
core:FASTFIGHTING.Lean.hostile: A choice for neutral tokens: taking no side, but leaning toward the enemy (they want the enemy's members safe).
core:FASTFIGHTING.Lean.closest: A choice for neutral tokens: taking no side, but each leaning toward whichever side is nearest it on the map.
core:FASTFIGHTING.Lean.underdog: A choice for neutral tokens: taking no side, but leaning toward whichever side is losing (it changes as the fight goes).
core:FASTFIGHTING.Lean.own: A choice for neutral tokens: they fight as a side of their own, against everyone.
